name: Payday itself, salary landed and posted today: the occurrence is closed and every real bill is deducted once (G362)

payday_plan present.reason: G362 closes the posted salary occurrence, so the plan loses its salary candidate and G172's landed-salary gate (_pp_salary_observed) never runs; the plan should be hidden once the salary has posted.

expected.notes: Payday itself, Fri 30 Oct 2026, pay period last Friday, so the new period runs 30 Oct to Thu 26 Nov (next payday Fri 27 Nov, 28 days away, window days 0 to 27). The 3,000 salary (history 31 Jul, 28 Aug and 25 Sep, equal, monthly rhythm, largest credit on Barclays) is the steady salary. Barclays holds 4,200 (1,200 before pay + 3,000 landed) and HSBC holds 80. Real items in the period: Barclays standing order to HSBC 900 (Fri 30 Oct, day 0, own account, HSBC spendable), mortgage 1,100 (Mon 2 Nov, day 3), council tax 150 (Fri 6 Nov, day 7), phone 45 (Mon 16 Nov, day 17); HSBC home insurance 120 (Tue 10 Nov, day 11). The salary has landed in the balance AND posted as an Income credit dated today (G362). The occurrence expected today is closed by that credit (same account, within 15 percent, inside the lookback), so no salary occurrence is left in the period (the next one is 31 days away, outside it) and the closed one is listed as observed income instead: nothing is credited a second time. Left to spend: pool 4,200 + 80 = 4,280. The standing order moves money inside the pool, so both of its legs drop. 4,280 - 1,100 = 3,180; - 150 = 3,030; - 120 = 2,910; - 45 = 2,865. There is no income left to credit. The lowest point is the last figure, 2,865, below the opening 4,280. No buffer, set-aside, goal or card reserve, so Left to spend is 2,865 (the real bills, 1,415, are deducted once). Barclays walk: 4,200 - 900 (day 0) = 3,300; - 1,100 = 2,200; - 150 = 2,050; - 45 = 2,005. After payments 2,005, low point 2,005, Spend from 2,005 (below the pool). HSBC walk: 80; the 900 standing order is credited on day 0 because its source is still at 3,300, at or above zero, after its own day-0 items (G360 funded rule), so 980; - 120 = 860. After payments 860; low point 80 (the opening balance is the lowest running balance); Spend from min(860, 80) = 80. Nobody is short, so no cover move; at risk 0. Payday plan, CORRECT: a salary credit has posted in this period, so the live plan has nothing left to recommend (G172) and there should be none. CURRENT behaviour, pinned: G362 closes the occurrence, so the plan no longer finds a salary candidate in the window (it reads upcoming_income), the landed-salary test that hides the plan (_pp_salary_observed) is never asked (it needs a candidate), and the plan stays on screen with a salary of 0, falling back to the current account with the most cash (Barclays, 4,200). Its sizing is then the same as the unposted scenario: Barclays keeps its bills excluding the own standing order, 1,100 + 150 + 45 = 1,295, plus the 50 buffer, so distributable 4,200 - 1,345 = 2,855; HSBC target 120 + 50 = 170 against 80, move 90; plan total 90 into HSBC. Known backend gap: payday_plan present (G362 against G172: the salary-observed gate needs the candidate the closed occurrence removed). It stops being a gap when the plan is hidden once the salary has posted.
